verdict.rationale: Honcho documents self-hosting: the open-source core can run on your own infrastructure, and `honcho start` brings up the API, deriver, Postgres and Redis locally via Docker. The MCP server can also run locally instead of using mcp.honcho.dev. However, it runs as a separate server stack rather than embedded in-process, and the 'custom' model option is never shown to mean local models, so independence from cloud LLM providers is unproven. Missing for 10: an in-process/embedded mode, documented support for local models (e.g. a local LLM backend for the deriver and reasoning), explicit confirmation of fully offline operation, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the memory layer fully locally — embedded in-process or against local models — without any cloud dependency

citations.quote: The core is open source at github.com/plastic-labs/honcho, so you can run the whole thing yourself and keep your data on your own infrastructure.
honcho start runs API, deriver, Postgres, and Redis via Docker.
Skip `mcp.honcho.dev` and run the MCP server locally over stdio, Streamable HTTP, or Docker.
